clue.text: Came to a funeral gathering with Edward

parts.note: a wake is the gathering of mourners around a death or funeral
Ned is a familiar short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Someone describes arriving at a funeral gathering in the company of a man called Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came to' reads as 'arrived at', but it is the definition in the sense of regaining consciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is to recover consciousness, which is to have stirred out of sleep or a faint.

clue.text: Frightens almost everyone with weapons

indicators.note: almost says the word for everyone stops one letter short

parts.note: all means everyone
arms are weapons

explanation.surface: Someone frightens nearly everybody by carrying guns.
explanation.definitionFit: To alarm someone is to scare them, a synonym of frighten.

clue.text: A pop group — one daughter's rejected

parts.note: a band is a pop group

explanation.surface: A pop group's daughter is rejected by its members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' is the definition; nothing is turned round here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abandoned has been cast aside, discarded or rejected.

clue.text: Look at fire rising over explosive device

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read the word for fire from bottom to top

parts.note: to axe someone is to fire them from a job
a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: An instruction to inspect a flame climbing above a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' looks like flames but means to sack; 'rising' reads it upwards (EXA) because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something is to inspect or study it closely.

clue.text: Go in emergency room below hospital department

indicators.note: in a down entry the emergency room letters sit under the department

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department
ER is emergency room

explanation.surface: Directions inside a hospital: enter the emergency room beneath another ward.
explanation.definitionFit: To go in is to come or pass into a place, a synonym of entering.

clue.text: Sample white wine, swallowing first bit of Rioja

indicators.note: the wine takes a letter into its mouth, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Mosel is a German white wine named after its river valley

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is the part used

explanation.surface: A wine taster tries a German white with a mouthful of Spanish red mixed in.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample in the sense of a small taste or tidbit is a tiny piece of food.

clue.text: One about to be restrained by tender policeman?

indicators.note: restrained means held in, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: to tender is to offer
I is the Roman numeral for one
C abbreviates circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone is about to be held back by a gentle policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' reads as gentle, but it is a verb: to offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer is a policeman; the question mark flags that officers also serve elsewhere.

clue.text: Set forth government position

definitions.meaning: to declare or express in words
a nation and its governing authority
a condition or situation, as in a sorry condition

explanation.surface: A list of phrases about laying out a government's position.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to declare, a nation's polity, and a condition one is in: three senses.

clue.text: Slack tie adult loosened

indicators.note: a loosened knot comes apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grown-up loosens his tie and leaves it slack.
explanation.definitionFit: Slack in the sense of leeway or freedom from strict limits.

clue.text: Widest track leading outside

indicators.note: the word for leading goes outside the track

parts.note: best means leading or top
a road is a track

explanation.surface: The widest track runs along the outside lane.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad means wide, so its superlative is the widest.

clue.text: In reality broadcast oafs attract fame

indicators.note: broadcast in the sense of scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A sneer at television: in real life, idiots on air become celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges all fifteen letters of OAFS ATTRACT FAME.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means actually or in truth, the same as saying something happens in reality.

clue.text: More incoherent male did rue getting drunk

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger about, so the words did rue are mixed up

explanation.surface: A man who regretted his drinking grows less coherent with every glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting drunk' rearranges DID RUE into UDDIER after M.
explanation.definitionFit: Muddy thinking or speech is confused and unclear, so a comparative of it means less coherent.

clue.text: Very old article by Conservative that is not without heart

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
i.e. abbreviates the Latin id est, meaning that is

indicators.note: the word not loses its central letter, its heart

explanation.surface: A rather prim comment on a very old piece of writing by a Tory that is not heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without heart' removes the middle O of NOT to leave NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ancient dates from long ago, a synonym of very old.

clue.text: Working with the church modus operandi — religious education again

parts.note: on means functioning or working, as a machine switched on
CE is the Church of England
MO abbreviates modus operandi, a way of working
RE is religious education, a British school subject

explanation.surface: A parish's method of working is to teach religion all over again.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the name of the school subject in Britain, taught in most state schools.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means one further time, a direct synonym of again.

clue.text: Facing work pressure over location

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
P is the symbol for pressure
O is over, the cricket abbreviation
a site is a location

explanation.surface: Facing pressure at work over where one is posted.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls in cricket, abbreviated O on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Two houses facing each other stand across from one another.

clue.text: People with diamonds bolted

parts.note: a race is a people sharing descent
D is the abbreviation for diamonds, the card suit

explanation.surface: Thieves carrying diamonds ran off.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolted in the sense of ran off at speed matches having sprinted.

clue.text: Chaos from prisoner marrying

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
fusion is a joining together, as two things are married

explanation.surface: Pandemonium breaks out when a convict marries.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorder and bewilderment amount to chaos.

clue.text: Standing very clear — it's exploding

indicators.note: the letters blow apart and land in a new order

parts.note: the word it with its 's, read as is, linking to the indicator

explanation.surface: A warning: something is very plainly standing ready to blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing' sits at the front looking like part of the surface, but it is the definition; 'exploding' gives ERTICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something standing is upright, at right angles to the ground.

clue.text: Some comprehend editor's wound up

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people grasp that the editor has been made angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound up' looks like agitated, but it is the definition in the sense of finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Wound up means brought to a close or concluded, a synonym of finished.

clue.text: Attractive woman with pay rise oddly lost money

parts.note: doll is slang for an attractive woman

indicators.note: the odd letters of the words pay rise go, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: An attractive woman's pay rise went astray.
explanation.definitionFit: The American currency unit, so a sum of them is money.

clue.text: Stroke bird's markings

parts.note: to pat is to stroke gently
a tern is a seabird; the bird's gives the word plus S

explanation.surface: An invitation to stroke the feathers of a bird showing its markings.
explanation.definitionFit: Patterns are the repeated designs or markings seen on fur, feathers or fabric.

clue.text: Former lover sat bare

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: An old flame sat naked for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare in the sense of uncovered and open to view.

clue.text: Where men might eat pickles

definitions.meaning: a military dining hall where service personnel take meals

explanation.surface: A question of where men might eat pickles.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names military dining halls and awkward predicaments, as in getting into a fix.

clue.text: Reptiles swagger around, encircling the Parisian

indicators.note: the turned piece goes around the French article, holding it inside
around says the word for swagger is turned the other way

parts.note: to strut is to swagger
le is French for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: Reptiles strut about a Parisian scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' gives TURTS, and 'encircling' makes the French article sit within it, before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Turtles are shelled reptiles, an example of the category.

clue.text: Right oven for joint?

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: Asking whether this is the right oven for cooking a joint of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: A joint is a large cut of meat cooked whole; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sunday roast is a large cut of meat cooked in the oven, so a joint is one.

clue.text: Take a picture badly — one's cut out

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the remaining letters are jumbled
cut out says a piece is removed from the words a picture

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bad photographer takes a picture with a person cropped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut out' removes an I from A PICTURE, and 'badly' rearranges APCTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a fortress or a prisoner is to seize it, the same as to seize by force.

clue.text: Evil scoundrels on ecstasy

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Wicked villains high on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: An evil in the sense of a scourge or affliction that blights people.

clue.text: Cleaner, polished car — it's nicest without new marks

parts.note: a char is a cleaning woman, short for charwoman

indicators.note: polished off or worked over, so these letters are reworked
without says a letter is removed from the words car it's nicest

explanation.surface: An advertisement for a cleaner who leaves a polished car without blemish.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is an old British name for a domestic cleaner. 'without' removes N from CARITSNICEST, and 'polished' rearranges the rest into ACTERISTICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinctive features or traits are the marks by which something is recognised.

clue.text: Most recent top grade is after student examination

indicators.note: the grade letter comes after the letter for the student

parts.note: L is a learner driver, used for a student
A is the highest grade
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: A student sitting a recent exam is chasing the top grade.
explanation.definitionFit: The newest or most up to date thing is the most recent.

clue.text: Legends in golf following leader with last of birdies

indicators.note: the in-golf piece follows the word for leader

parts.note: a head is a leader
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Golf legends follow the tournament leader, who closes with birdies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legends' suggests great players, but it is the definition: captions or titles.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend can be the caption or title text over a map or picture, a synonym for titles.
